items.title: The 10 client emails I stopped rewriting (free templates inside)
items.pt:
Every freelancer has a folder of emails they rewrite from scratch. Mine had 40 drafts of the same three sentences.

Last month I finally sat down and wrote them out properly. Ten of them cover almost everything.


  
  
  The ten




Cold outreach that does not sound like a pitch - one specific observation, one line of proof, one question.

The follow-up that adds value - a new idea, not "just checking in".

Scope confirmation - the one that prevents revision hell. Send it before you start.

The

items.title: Data manager cover letter, with an example you can adapt
items.pt:
Key takeaways


A data manager cover letter should tell one story about a data standard you set and got other people to follow, because that's the part of the job a resume can't show. Your resume already lists the warehouse, the catalog and the reporting tools, so use the letter to explain who resisted the rule, how you got them on board and what got better.

items.title: WARN Act and Your Property Taxes — What Happens When Your Paycheck Stops
items.pt: A WARN notice tells you your job is ending, but your property tax bill does not shrink when your paycheck does. Property taxes are set by your county or city from your home's assessed value and the local tax rate; your income is not part of the formula. The median U.S. bill was $3,500 in 2024, according to Realtor.com's analysis of Census data, roughly $290 a month, arriving on schedule while your income does not. items.title: What I charge as a one-person IT consultant in Germany (real numbers)
items.pt:
I have been freelancing in Germany for a few years. Rates are the thing everyone asks about and nobody publishes. So here are mine.


  
  
  The numbers



Hourly: 85 EUR for small jobs, 95 EUR for anything that needs a contract.
Day rate: 680 EUR (8 hours, on site in Braunschweig or remote).
Retainer: 1,200 EUR per month for 2 days of availability plus email support.
Fixed price projects: estimate hours, multiply by 95, add 20 percent. That 20 percent is not greed, it is the cost of the things

items.pt: We present MEMO (a Mesh for Every MOment), a method that reconstructs the geometry of complete dynamic scenes, captured by multiple synchronized cameras, and extracts a mesh at every frame. items.pt: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. items.title: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
